units.text: Choose Document D B for a managed document workload only after proving that your application works with its supported Mongo D B APIs. This instance-based example uses a primary, reader replicas, and distributed storage across three Availability Zones.

Managed storage and backups reduce operational work. They do not make compatibility automatic. Check the engine version and deployment type, then validate your actual drivers, queries and transactions before migration.
Use the real application to test compatibility before committing. The illustrated primary handles writes; replicas can serve reads when the client is configured for that read path.

Run through authentication and T L S, query operators and indexes, then transactions. Simulate a primary failure and measure reconnect time and latency; a successful connection alone does not establish compatibility.

Compare storage configurations with representative reads and writes. On supported instance-based clusters, Standard adds per-request I O charges to instance and storage charges. I O-Optimized removes the per-operation charge, not the instance or storage charges.

Reader replicas still add compute cost. Include backup storage, data transfer and growth in the estimate. A steady, I O-heavy workload is a candidate for I O-Optimized, but verify it with current regional pricing.
A time-series database helps answer questions like average temperature per site over fifteen minutes. Each record combines event time, dimensions such as device or site, and a measured value.

LiveAnalytics closed to new customers in June 2025; this does not end service for existing eligible users. For a new design, evaluate Timestream for Influx D B against your ingestion, query and retention needs. Do not assume the products share APIs or tiers.

Build the measurement around what you need to query. This observation identifies device and site, records two readings, and retains the timestamp. Grouping by site or device across a time window answers a different question from fetching one document.

The historical LiveAnalytics example uses S Q L. If you are building with Influx D B instead, choose and test the supported query interface for that engine and version. Do not carry over the historical sample unchanged.

Prove that the dashboard can query an event, not merely that the stream accepted it. Track one synthetic device observation through Kinesis, processing, and the selected time-series store to the consumer.

Replay an event and send a late one. Inspect deduplication, timestamp handling and retention, then verify accepted writes, failed records and the actual query result. Use supported clients for the chosen engine rather than assuming identical integrations.

Prove the Dynamo D B key design before scaling. In a sandbox, query the USER number 42 partition with sort keys beginning with GAME. Compare consumed capacity and pagination with a broader Scan; a Query response can still require another page.

When the application must look up all users for a game, test a global secondary index keyed by game I D. Wait until the index is active and verify its eventually consistent query results. Using Scan for every game lookup is not the same access pattern.

Measure recovery with a real restore in a sandbox, not merely a completed snapshot. Verify the recovery point, engine version and key access, then restore a new private instance with the required subnets and security groups.

Connect to that instance and prove that representative application operations succeed. Only then update the sandbox application endpoint, record elapsed time and preserve a rollback decision. A successful restore A P I call is not a successful application recovery.

Use a controlled concurrent burst to test whether R D S Proxy reduces database connections. Configure a supported target, private reachability and a supported authentication path before adding representative client load.

Measure client connections, database connections, latency and session pinning together. Do not expect one database connection for all clients. Test an authorized sandbox failure, restore the configuration and clean up.
Demonstrate cache-aside with product 42. The first read misses, reads version one from the database and fills the cache. The next request hits the cached copy without that database read.

When the database changes to version two, the cache can keep returning version one until expiration or invalidation. Verify the next read refreshes it. Then check controlled fallback to the database without overloading it.

Select the S three data transfer feature for your Aurora engine. MySQL uses LOAD DATA FROM S three for import and select INTO OUTFILE S three for export. PostgreSQL uses the A W S S three extension functions shown for the same two directions.

Confirm engine and version support, network access, I A M and any relevant K M S permissions, and database grants. Test with a small file and check the resulting rows. Import or export is data movement, not a transactional recovery plan.

Subscribe to R D S events to start investigation, not to declare recovery. Select a source and categories such as failover or configuration, route through an S N S topic, and confirm the subscriber actually receives a notification.

If a failover event arrives, check the current writer and prove the application can reconnect. Use CloudWatch metrics for performance symptoms and logs for query or audit evidence. Delivery may lag, so use current resource state for the decision.
